$comment: The one source of truth. Add a game = one entry here + one 1280x800 webp in shots/. Then run `node build.mjs`. Only status "published" is rendered and allowed in frame-src.

Tidepool.title: Tidepool, two ways
Tidepool.line: The same evolving sea twice. In Tidepool you watch it and nudge the water; in Red Queen you harvest it, and it adapts to how you play.

games.title: FOUNDRY
games.subtitle: A Question of Severance
games.oneLine: A turn-based roguelike: you are a maintenance robot waking inside a factory that sealed its doors and severed its staff nineteen years ago.
blurb: You come back online in Maren's workshop in Gatetown, a shanty grown against the factory wall. The bench is cold and the door is open.

Every move is a turn. Search, pick up what the heaps give you, fit it to your paper doll, and watch integrity and charge. Saves live in the game's own storage, and the in-game export writes them to a file.
controls: Arrow keys or h j k l

mobile.note: Needs a keyboard. It has no touch controls, and its title screen is clipped at phone width. Best on a computer.

sandboxWhy.allow-same-origin: Gives the game its own origin (never the hub's) so its saves in localStorage work.
sandboxWhy.allow-pointer-lock: Kept from the reviewed base set the game was first framed with. Not used today and harmless.
sandboxWhy.allow-downloads: The save export writes a JSON file through an <a download> click. Without it that silently fails inside the frame.

games.reason: Live at its Vercel URL; frames from another origin (no X-Frame-Options or CSP).

screenshot.alt: FOUNDRY in play: a robot standing in a wooden workshop in Gatetown, with integrity, charge and systems panels on the right.

games.madeWith: HTML canvas and plain JavaScript, no framework

games.title: Word From Below
games.oneLine: A season at the Downward Tower: you keep the books at the head of the pit, send parties down with written orders, and decide which of their reports to believe.
blurb: You are the Factor at the head of the pit. Parties go down with your written orders and come back with reports, and not every line in a report is true.
Mark each line trusted, doubted or rejected, and keep the stores, the map and the people straight across a six-week season.
controls: Choose, mark a line, open a room

mobile.note: Touch-first on phones, with a bottom tab bar for the six sections.

sandboxWhy.allow-same-origin: Its save and settings live in localStorage, and its module scripts must load from its own origin.
sandboxWhy.allow-forms: The seed field and the room rename are forms whose submit handlers call preventDefault; without it Enter in the seed field would not start a season.

games.reason: Waiting for its Vercel project. Its vercel.json must also list https://games.michaelking.systems in frame-ancestors (branch hub-framing in word_from_below).

screenshot.alt: Word From Below in play: the Reports section open on a week 2 debrief from Bessa Thorn, each line marked trusted, beside the section rail.

games.madeWith: Plain JavaScript ES modules, no framework

games.title: Tidepool
games.oneLine: A small ocean that runs itself: creatures with genomes graze, breed, mutate and die, and you only nudge the water.
blurb: A closed ecosystem. Every creature carries a genome of speed, perception, size and restlessness, and pays a metabolic price for its gifts. Nothing is scripted; whatever the pool looks like in ten minutes, it evolved that way.
Drop nutrients, stir a current, or call a storm. The pool hums if you turn the sound on, and its pitch follows the population. It is a toy more than a game: there is no score and no end.

mobile.note: Works on phones: tap and drag both act on the water, and nothing scrolls sideways at 390 px. The trait panel is hidden on narrow screens.

sandboxWhy.allow-scripts: The game is one HTML file with an inline script. It keeps nothing in storage, so it runs in an opaque origin without allow-same-origin.

games.reason: Live at its Vercel URL; frames from another origin (no X-Frame-Options or CSP), verified in a sandboxed iframe on the local server.

screenshot.alt: Tidepool running: glowing creatures in many colours drifting among green plants on a dark sea, with the stats panel for The Quiet Basin at bottom left.

games.madeWith: One HTML file: canvas 2D and Web Audio

games.title: Red Queen
games.oneLine: A co-evolutionary harvest game: every strike is natural selection, so the pool learns you. Herd its genome into a corner, then exploit the open flank.
blurb: The Tidepool sea again, but now you fish it. Three tools each catch a different kind of creature and breed the opposite trait: the Net breeds speed, the Lure breeds guile, the Jolt breeds nerve. Lean on one and the pool's other flanks open.

A run lasts three and a half minutes. Each tide you draft one of three powers. Push a trait to its corner to trigger a bloom, then cash the flanks it left open. There is a daily challenge with a shared seed.

mobile.note: Plays with taps on a phone. At 390 px the tool bar loses a few pixels at each edge, and the power draft shows only its middle card in full; the other two run off the screen.

sandboxWhy.allow-scripts: The game is one HTML file with an inline script. It keeps nothing in storage, so it runs in an opaque origin without allow-same-origin.

allowWhy.clipboard-write: The end screen's Copy result button writes the run summary to the clipboard. Without this permission the copy is blocked, though the button still says Copied.

games.reason: Live at its Vercel URL; frames from another origin (no X-Frame-Options or CSP), verified in a sandboxed iframe on the local server.

screenshot.alt: Red Queen in play: a pale sea of creatures around the Lure's gold strike ring, score 732 at the top, the gene-pool triangle at bottom left and the Net, Lure and Jolt cards along the bottom.

games.madeWith: One HTML file: canvas 2D and Web Audio
